title: STATIC_CALLED_ON_INSTANCE (or similar) does not appear when accessing a static property via an instance
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.5.dev.custom_build [f0f88f7b8]

### System information

Godot v4.5.dev (f0f88f7b8) - macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Pro - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads)

### Issue description

The warning `STATIC_CALLED_ON_INSTANCE` appears when attempting to call a static function via an instance of a class rather than the class itself:
```gdscript
extends Node

class MathFuncs:
    static func subtract_two(val):
        return val - 2

func _ready():
    var my_math_funcs = MathFuncs.new()
    # Will give warning STATIC_CALLED_ON_INSTANCE.
    var result = my_math_funcs.subtract_two(5)
```

However, no such warning is emitted when attempting to access a static property/variable of a class via an instance:
```gdscript
extends Node

class MathFuncs:
    static var pi = 3.14

func _ready():
    var my_math_funcs = MathFuncs.new()
    my_math_funcs.pi  # No warning for accessing via instance. 
```

It seems to me like the concerns with accessing functions would also apply to accessing variables/properties. Perhaps even more so, since a user could reasonably expect different instances to have independent values:
```gdscript
extends Node

class MyNumbers:
    static var num = 0

func _ready():
    var my_nums_1 = MyNumbers.new()
    var my_nums_2 = MyNumbers.new()

    my_nums_1.num = 3
    my_nums_2.num = 4

    # Prints "First num is 4, second num is 4"
    print("First num is %s, second num is %s" % [my_nums_1.num, my_nums_2.num])
```

### Steps to reproduce

Paste the snippets above into a GDScript file in a Godot project and view the warnings.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Provided as scripts above.
